correct markup, no number. A selector check would have passed.
Queue 33's 30-second glance: the strip line carries the figure the fits badge was measured
against. A card that reads 'worst case fits' with no number is a verdict the operator has
to raise the card to audit -- the click the glance exists to remove. Asserted on the strip
(.pers-strip), not the card body, so the badge and the number are on the same line.
Queue 33 (plan §6.14.1t): the reason, on the line the verdict is on.
A strip that reads 'does not fit' has told the operator the bad half and stopped;
the reason (which of the two ceilings, by how much, or which models are unpriceable)
was computed and carried in the payload and printed nowhere. In this sandbox every
card fits, so the assertion is the negative: a fitting card carries NO reason clause.
That is a real guard -- a reason printed unconditionally is how a verdict with no
defect ends up labelled as one, and the per-card attribution rule (the strip printed
the NEXT card's figure) applies to sentences exactly as it applies to numbers.
Plan 6.14.1u: one verdict per strip, and the verdict answers BOTH ceilings.
The badge used to answer the aperture only, so a card the validator puts over
physical RAM was badged green -- and an OOM the kernel delivers is exactly what
that looks like on this box, not a GPU error. The live sandbox fits both
ceilings, so the page's assertion is the count: a badge per strip, and the
running badge is the second one a strip is allowed. The five states themselves
(over RAM, over the aperture, unpriced, unmeasurable, fits) are forced in
tests/test_personality_routes.py, where the badge WORDS are asserted against a
table -- a page harness can only see the state the sandbox happens to be in.
A strip's sentence names the card it judges. The deck has already printed a
neighbour's NUMBER (6.14.1s, loop.index against a 0-ordered list); the same
class of bug applies to sentences, and a guard that reads only the badge and
reason spans cannot see it -- the card name lives outside those spans. The
state guard asserts name-in-strip per card; this pins it on the live page.
Asserted as the strip's own first span, not as deck-wide text, because
textOf-style deck text always contains every card's name.

_comment: The handoff (queue 32): Launch is not a sentence on the list page, it is the page's switch
into the session it opened. The row's button, the personality named by the select, and the
operational view becoming the page are asserted together, because the defect this queue is
about is precisely a launch that reports success and leaves the operator on the list holding
a session id.
Quit leaves the operational state and returns to the list, with the session id in the
sentence — the session stays open on the host, so the page to go to next is the harness
page. Quit is confirm-gated, so the sweep's dialog-refused pass must leave the view up and
the accepted pass must land the exit.
Quit is asserted before the send case, because it leaves the view: the list's summary line
The case runs the click; the page's state after quitting is measured by the launch case that
follows it, which only passes if the list row offers Launch again.
Quit goes back to the list, so the row's Launch verb is back; launching again is the page
re-opening the session the host still holds. The list row's Launch and the served state are
the same handoff the first case asserts.
The send box is the page's own verb, aimed at the session the page is showing: it names the
project, not a session id the operator copied. Text typed into it, then Send, must reach the
agent — read below as the host's answer and the transcript that grows.
sec 6.14.1n: the projects page. It shows a shortlist of checkboxes and a plan, and every
promise it makes about them is a promise about the server: a missing toolchain is refused
by name, a plan creates nothing, forgetting deletes nothing. Launch is the harness page's
session view (sec 6.14.1m); queue 33 gave this page a launch verb of its own, so Launch acts:
it posts to /api/projects/launch, records the session with the personality it runs with, and
is disabled by the host's answer read off the payload — not by a literal, so it flips when the
host does. The sweep drives the fields and the buttons; the assertions below are the outcomes
the operator reads. Launch needs no confirm() from the sweep: it opens a session, deletes
nothing, and the endpoint carries its own confirm field.

requireConfirmFor names the forget endpoint: the sweep accepts confirm() in its second pass, so a page that posts /api/projects/forget without asking is caught there. Create and adopt need no confirm (registry writes, nothing on disk deleted) and the endpoint says so.

and the scan lists folders the portal did not author. A hostile folder name is a
stored-XSS payload that arrives by `git clone`.

host never runs in the sandbox. So the sweep drives the payload's launch state, supplied here:
the page reads launch.available off the payload and enables the row's button from it, then
posts to the endpoint the payload names. The fixture is the host's answer, not a convenience -

it, so the page is exercised with the shape the endpoint answers. The personality list carries
